# Testament of Zebulun — 6
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Zebulun's testimony is about compassion — the kind that breaks open inside you when you witness someone else's suffering. His was triggered by Joseph.

**1** He was 114 years old when he gathered his sons. He said:

**2** I am Zebulun. I don't have much to confess. The only real wrong I did was staying silent about Joseph — agreeing with my brothers to keep the secret from our father. My brothers had sworn: if anyone tells, we kill him. So I stayed quiet. But I wept for Joseph in private, for a long time.

**3** And when they wanted to actually kill him — when Simeon and Gad went after him — I threw myself on the ground and begged them not to do it.

**4** I heard Joseph beg for his life. He was weeping. He said: Have mercy on me, brothers. Think of our father Jacob. I haven't sinned against you — and even if I have, punish me, don't kill me. For our father's sake.

**5** Something broke open in me when he said that. I began weeping too. My whole body shook. Joseph wept and I wept and it felt like the earth itself was trembling.

**6** I stepped up and said: We are not killing him. We'll throw him in a dry well. God forbid we should destroy our own brother.

**7** But Simeon and Gad held him anyway. They pushed me aside and accused Joseph of spying. Then Judah took him away. And while Judah was gone, the Midianite traders came and pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver.

**8** We were ashamed. We slaughtered a kid and dipped Joseph's robe in the blood and brought it to Jacob. Our father mourned for years.

**9** And so did I — inwardly. After that day, something changed in me. The sound of Joseph crying, begging, stayed with me. And I decided: from that day forward, I would have compassion on anyone who suffers.

**10** I gave bread to the hungry. I gave clothes to the naked. I helped the sick. I helped strangers. I did it because I had heard what helplessness sounds like.

**11** Now hear me, sons: love the LORD with all your strength and love each other in truth.

**12** Here is what I have learned: hardness of heart is where all evil is born. A man with a hard heart sins against God and against people. He takes from others. He turns away from the crying. **13** But a man with compassion — even if he is poor — is rich before God. A man with money and a hard heart — he is poor before God, no matter what he owns.

**14** Compassion is a gift from God. If you have it, God will have compassion on you. If you don't, you will be alone.

**15** Measure it this way: the compassion you show your neighbors is the compassion God shows you. Exactly that much. No more.

**16** When we came to Egypt and saw Joseph again — he bore no bitterness toward us. He loved us. He gave us everything. That is what compassion looks like when it has been fully grown.

**17** So, sons: love God. Love each other. Feed the hungry. Be moved by suffering. Don't look away from the poor or the stranger. Because if you do, God will give you hardness in return, and no prayer will soften it.

**18** After saying this, Zebulun died in peaceful old age. His sons buried him in Hebron with his fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Zebulun*
